To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) HMDs can detect malware with high accuracy, (b) the hardware footprint of malware is large, and (c) obfuscation techniques can help HMDs.

(1) HMDs can be designed to be less intrusive than prior techniques and yet be more effective, (2) obfuscation techniques that are used by malware to hide from static analyzers can be leveraged to make HMDs more effective.

1) small atomic actions, like stealing a Contact or a SMS, have surprisingly big hardware footprints and 2) obfuscation techniques that make malware harder to detect in static analyses make them more detectable with HMDs.
